message.content:
Here are a few highly regarded documentaries that explore global warming and climate change:

| Title | Year | Synopsis |
|-------|------|----------|
| **“An Inconvenient Truth”** | 2006 | Former Vice‑President Al Gore’s presentation on climate science, featuring interviews, data visualizations, and a personal narrative. |
| **“An Inconvenient Sequel: Truth to Power”** | 2017 | A follow‑up that examines progress (or lack thereof) since the first film, with new footage from the Paris Agreement negotiations. |
| **“Before the Flood”** | 2016 | Leonardo DiCaprio travels around the world to witness the impacts of climate change, interviewing scientists, activists, and policymakers. |
| **“Climate Change: The Facts”** | 2019 | A BBC production that breaks down the science, economics, and politics behind global warming, using clear graphics and expert interviews. |
| **“The 11th Hour”** | 2007 | A documentary that looks at the environmental crisis from a global perspective, featuring voices from the UN, scientists, and activists. |
| **“Our Planet” (Season 1)** | 2019 | While primarily a nature series, the first season includes extensive coverage of how climate change is affecting ecosystems worldwide. |

All of these are available on major streaming platforms such as Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Hulu, or can be rented/bought on iTunes/Google Play. If you’d like more details on any particular film or help finding where to watch it, just let me know!
